With the Commander's ascension and control of the Worldwound, the threat to the mortal realm was ended, and Nocticula vanished from the Abyss. She later reappeared in Elysium among the Azata, having somehow ascended to godhood. When asked how she had managed such a feat, Nocticula would only offer a satisfied chuckle. Taking the moniker of the Redeemer Queen, she set about forming her new realm, the Midnight's Palette.

Many rumors and half-truths were sorted through as Nocticula's' followers began to build a new canon for her church. One rumor that found its way into the discourse was a story about a relationship between Nocticula and the Commander. Perhaps no longer seeing a reason to hide it or perhaps merely to sow some chaos, Nocticula chose to confirm this story. It would not be long till the two nascent churches would begin intertwining, in more ways than one.

The other Empyreal Lords welcomed the news of their relationship. They viewed the Commander as their brethren, and hoped that the relationship between the two would help ease Nocticula's transition from Demon Lord.

As a fellow ascended former Demon, Arushalae would often speak with Nocticula wishing to support each other in their transition. In time a loving (or perhaps lustful) relationship would blossom between Arushalae and Nocticula, which they would share with the Commander.

The other Empyreal Lords welcomed the news of their relationship. While the Commander was not an Azata, the Commander's soul was full of light, which Nocticula needed. The Empyreal Lords hoped that the relationship between the two would help ease Nocticula's transition from Demon Lord.

The other Empyreal Lords welcomed the news of their relationship. While the Commander was not an Azata, the Commander's soul was full of the same chaos they all shared. The Empyreal Lords hoped that the relationship between the two would help ease Nocticula's transition from Demon Lord.

The other Empyreal Lords were ambivalent about the news of the relationship. While they respected the Commander for closing the Worldwound, the order within the Commander's soul was at odds with both Nocticula's nature and their own. They worried that that unbendable order might someday break Nocticula. They mostly held their tongues though as the two seemed to be happy together at least for now.

The other Empyreal Lords objected to the relationship. The Commander was the antithesis to all that they were. The Commander would not be allowed in Elysium. The relationship between the two continued, mostly in the Commander's personal plane, but many obstacles remained for the two.

True to her word, Nocticula invited Laulieh to join her when she left the Abyss. Still enamored with the Commander, the succubus agreed to follow her mistress. The demon serves as Nocticula's aide while struggling with her new surroundings. Oftentimes she is sent as a liaison between Nocticula and the Commander, a position that brings her great pleasure. The Azata keep a close eye on Laulieh waiting to see whether she will someday find her better nature or need to be banished from Elysium for falling back on old habits.

With Nocticula's ascension and Shamira's death, a power vacuum formed in the Midnight Isles. Several powerful demons arrived seeking to claim to masterless realm. However before any of them could make a move to claim the throne, the realm itself had recognized the Commander as its ruler. "I believe my mythic power can pierce the darkness, could you transform Terendelev's scale for me?"

{n}Storyteller moves his finger along the surface of the scale tracing magic runes, soon the traced patterns glow as the magic of the scale is reconfigured. He returns the scale to you once more.{/n} "Focus on the scale when you wish to try and pierce the darkness."
"I'd to know how someone in Golarion is doing."
"I will tell you what I know."
"That's everyone I wanted to ask about for now."
"Let me know if you want to ask about anyone else."
"Have you heard anything about how Nurah is doing?"

"To the best of my knowledge, she hasn't been in Drezen in some time. The last I heard of her was when she arrived in the war room looking for you. She found Galfrey and learned of your mission to the Abyss." {n}The Storyteller lightly chuckles.{/n} "I believe nearly half of Drezen heard the shriek that followed."
"Have you encountered Targona?"
"I came across her after my initial return. She asked a favor of me, but that can wait till you finish your task."
"I came across her after my initial return. She seemed concerned about something and asked a favor, but that can wait till you finish your task."
"Ah yes, I need to talk to you about a favor she asked of me when you have finished your other business with me."
"I don't believe she has been around."
"How is Aranka doing?"

"There have been some... disagreements between her and Galfrey. The Free Crusaders have been spending less time in Drezen as a result. Aranka still comes by occasionally to see if you have returned yet or to ask me about magical artifacts. I'll tell her I saw you next time I encounter her."
"Has someone named Aranka stopped by Drezen?"

"Oh yes, I met her recently when she stopped by the city. She said she was looking to speak with you. We had a chat about magical artifacts when we met. I'll be sure to tell her I saw you if she stops by again."
"Anyone in town I should know about?"
"That's all I can think of at the moment."
"I'll follow up later."
"I'll be here."

"Nurah stopped by looking for you earlier. She asked me about the devils that now roam the city. She sounded quite distraught when I told her that they were following you. I don't know where she went, but with the amount of cursing, I suspect she won't be returning."
"Let me see that paper."
"Nurah came by earlier to give me a sheet of paper. I don't know what is on it, but I can tell there are strong emotions for you imbued into it."

"I encountered Targona in the city earlier, but she sounded sad. She asked me to tell you that she couldn't see you anymore. That she didn't recognize the brave {mf|man|woman} that saved her anymore."
"I encountered Targona in the city earlier, but she sounded sad. She asked me to tell you that she wouldn't be dropping by anymore. The city is too sad for her..."
[Go look for Targona]
"Targona has apparently been frequenting the Half Measure recently if you are looking for her."
[Investigate the 'ghost' sightings]
"I've heard some of your troops talking about the 'ghost of Minagho' haunting part of Drezen."
[Speak with 'Mina']
"A woman calling herself Mina stopped by earlier and asked me to tell you to meet her in the Half Measure."
[Speak with Minagho]
"Mina came by again asking to speak with you once again."
"You should know that I have been speaking with someone who believes themselves to be Terendelev. She doesn't know where she is or how she got there."

{n}The dragon raises his head in surprise.{/n} "Well that is certainly an interesting lie for someone to create." {n}He closes his eyes in thought.{/n} "But if it is really her, that might explain why she hasn't responded to the clerics that have attempted to bring her back."
"I'm afraid I can't give you any advice regarding what this 'Terendelev' is as I have not heard anything from her. Regardless of whether it is Terendelev though, I hope you will help this lost soul. And if it is my beloved apprentice, please remind her that despite her self-doubts, I will always be proud of her."
"Terendelev's soul was apparently shattered, and I've been speaking to part of her soul while the rest was bound to her skeleton."
"I see. I suppose the reason she couldn't be brought back was because of that undead. I'm glad you could help at least a portion of her."
"She's told me as much. I'm glad you could provide enough help that she was able to return to us."
"I thought you should know that I have begun a courtship with Terendelev."
"She mentioned that to me as well. I'm happy for the two of you. I hope you can support each other in any trials that are to come."
"What happened to Hulrun?"

"He resigned from his positions of prelate and governor before turning himself in claiming he had abused his power. It was quite a shock in Kenabres. He is scheduled to receive a proper trial in the capital as there were concerns over whether he could get a fair hearing in Kenabres."

"The former prelate was indeed known for his fervor, as you say. He was harsh in his judgments and hasty in his punishments. As he saw it, it was better for an innocent to die than an enemy to survive. I wouldn't go so far as to call his view heretical — if that were true, the goddess would revoke her blessing from him... But still, it is unbefitting a servant of Iomedae to adhere to the letter of the law so stringently. Iomedae is a goddess of good, and even her inquisitor should be guided by love for his fellow beings."

"Chun Dawei. I commanded the guards of Kenabres. After Prelate Hulrun's resignation, I became the governor. Officially, I still hold that position, though I've been fighting in Drezen for nearly a year."
"I'd never betray my love!"

"Ah yes, I had an inkling that you and Aranka were sleeping together. But is that love truly reciprocated? Are you sure she won't just abandon you the next time she sees someone she finds attractive? Chaotic whims just hurt everyone. But if you agree to my contract, I'll throw in a bonus and make sure she can never leave you."
"What about Aranka?"

"Whatever feelings you harbor for her, I won't make an exception for her. I doubt she would be very appreciative even if I did. However, if you agree to my contract, I'll throw in a bonus and make sure she can never leave you."
"What about Aranka?"

"Our contract is null, but I am a devil of my word." {n}Mephistoles holds up a black sapphire gem.{/n} "With her soul trapped in this gem, she can never leave you again. At least not by choice." {n}An imp appears from behind him and grabs the gem before flying off.{/n} "I'll be holding on to that. I might have failed at my primary goal, but stopping a Dream Warden from spreading chaos is at least a small victory."
"What about Aranka?"

"Of course, I didn't forget about the signing bonus I included." {n}Mephistoles hands you a black sapphire gem.{/n} "I bound her soul while you were fighting the other rabble. Now everything that she was will forever be yours. I wouldn't recommend freeing her, she'd certainly refuse any attempts to resurrect her after that display. Give it a few centuries though, and I'm sure you'll find some use for her soul after you've grown bored of holding onto that trinket."
